title: Quentin and the Ghost
premise: August Lockridge, a financial-crimes investigator who launders the reputations of the powerful, receives a calendar invite from Marcus Vane — their handler, dead for six months. The meeting pulls them into a conspiracy to stage a catastrophic 'accident' at a decommissioned refinery, disguised as an insurance write-off worth billions. Guided by Vane's posthumous breadcrumbs and an uneasy alliance with the ghost's estranged daughter, August must expose the plot without becoming its next erased line item. In the end, August chooses justice outside the law, burning their own clean-money empire to bury the conspirators in evidence they can't launder.
about_author: Bram Sterling is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people who discover that paper trails are just ghosts waiting to be summoned.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: August Lockridge scrubs a senator's ledger until it gleams, then freezes: a calendar invite from Marcus Vane, dead six months, for tomorrow at 9 a.m. POV August. The beat is cold dread beneath professional calm — the first crack in a life built on plausible deniability.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: August investigates the invite through back channels and finds Vane's death certificate authentic, his accounts closed, his digital footprint professionally erased — by someone very good. POV August. The emotional beat is denial curdling into obsession; they can't stop pulling the thread.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock
chapters.summary: At the meeting address — a shuttered notary office — August finds no Vane, only a burner phone ringing on the desk and a folder labeled with August's real name, which almost no one knows. POV August. The beat is vertigo: someone has been inside their identity all along.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Daughter
chapters.summary: The phone leads to Nadia Vane, who received the same invitation and assumes August killed her father. A hostile standoff becomes wary truce when they compare notes: both were given coordinates to the Meridian refinery. POV alternates August/Nadia. The beat is friction sparking into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Surveillance of the refinery reveals a scheduled 'safety inspection' in eleven days, followed by an insurance valuation — and a new subsidiary quietly formed by the Halcyon Group. POV Nadia. The beat is dawning horror as she recognizes her father's handwriting in the margin notes of a leaked schematic.

chapters.title: What Vane Knew
chapters.summary: A dead-drop message from Vane's account surfaces: a partial list of names and the phrase 'the accident is the asset.' August realizes the attack isn't sabotage — it's a business model. POV August. The beat is grim clarity; the crime is legal-shaped, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Old Contacts
chapters.summary: August approaches a disgraced actuary who once flagged Meridian's risk profile and finds him freshly terrified, packing to flee. He gives them one name — Director Edda Marsh of Halcyon — before his car brakes fail on a dry road. POV August. The beat is guilt: asking questions got a man killed.

chapters.title: Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: Nadia decodes her father's hidden files and learns he discovered the scheme, faked nothing, and died anyway — his death repackaged as heart failure by the same team now staging Meridian. POV Nadia. The beat is grief weaponized; she stops mourning and starts hunting.

chapters.title: The Tailor
chapters.summary: August identifies the conspiracy's fixer, a man called the Tailor who manufactures accidents, and arranges a meeting under a false identity. The Tailor sees through it instantly but lets August leave alive — a message, not mercy. POV August. The beat is terror laced with dark exhilaration at being seen.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Within hours, August's accounts freeze, their credentials rot, and their firm disavows them. The machine that cleaned money for others begins erasing its own. POV August. The beat is identity collapse — stripped of every alias, August must decide who remains underneath.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Holed up with Nadia, August maps the conspiracy: seven names, five days, one refinery. They argue over whether to go to authorities, knowing three of the seven sit in oversight positions. POV alternating. The beat is found family forming in extremis — two strangers becoming each other's only trusted witness.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Vane's list resolves: the fifth conspirator is August's own mentor, Ilsa Brandt, who taught them that clean money is a kindness. Confronting her, August gets a partial confession recorded — then watches her walk free, untouchable, smiling. POV August. The beat is betrayal sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: The Tailor's crew moves equipment into Meridian under inspection cover. Nadia infiltrates the contractor roster while August traces the trigger mechanism — a gas release timed to look like corrosion failure. POV Nadia. The beat is claustrophobic tension as she realizes workers will be on-site during the 'accident.'

chapters.title: Collateral
chapters.summary: August discovers the plan requires casualties for the insurance math: twelve night-shift contractors are the deductible. The abstract crime becomes bodies with names. POV August. The beat is moral rupture — this stopped being about money the moment lives became line items.

chapters.title: Turning the Ghost
chapters.summary: A final Vane message reveals his last move: a dead-man's switch holding full evidence, keyed to a passphrase only Nadia would know — her childhood nickname. But triggering it also exposes how Vane bent rules for years. POV Nadia. The beat is a daughter choosing her father whole, flaws included.

chapters.title: The Trap They Built
chapters.summary: August and Nadia realize the invitation was never a rescue call — Vane planned for them to be inside Meridian when it happened, patsies for the accident. The trap closes as security locks down the site early. POV August. The beat is betrayal beyond the grave, and the choice to use the trap anyway.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Inside the refinery, August and Nadia race to disable the gas-release assembly while the doomed contractor crew works unknowingly around them. A Tailor operative hunts them through the pipe galleries. POV alternating. The beat is white-knuckle suspense — sabotage as rescue.

chapters.title: What Burns
chapters.summary: They fail to fully disarm the mechanism but vent the plume and force an evacuation, saving the crew as a contained fireball erupts — an accident that looks like an accident, minus the deaths. POV Nadia. The beat is exhausted triumph shadowed by knowledge that the conspirators will spin even this.

chapters.title: The Switch
chapters.summary: With the site compromised, Halcyon moves to destroy records. Nadia triggers Vane's dead-man's switch from a diner booth, releasing everything to regulators, journalists, and the seven conspirators themselves. POV Nadia. The beat is quiet ferocity — the ghost speaks at last, and everyone hears.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Marsh and four others are arrested as the evidence avalanche lands; Brandt attempts flight and is taken at the border; the Tailor vanishes, leaving a single calling card for August. POV August. The beat is justice arriving sideways — imperfect, partial, earned outside the law.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Testifying under immunity, August torches their own career and clean-money practice, naming the industry's machinery from the stand. Nadia offers them a role in a nonprofit auditing whistleblower cases. POV August. The beat is rebirth — identity rebuilt from what survived the fire.

chapters.title: Quentin and the Ghost
chapters.summary: Months later, August — going by Quentin, the name on their original birth certificate — meets Nadia at Vane's grave. A new calendar invite arrives from an unknown sender: another accident being scheduled. They exchange a look, and say yes together. POV Quentin. The beat is open-eyed continuation: the found family has work to do.
